messages:
Anya Patel: Quick brain-dump from this morning's roadmap sync — I'm using a dumb analogy: think of routing policies as 'railroad switches'. We want clear switch positions (regionally isolated, shared pool, fallback) and a visible safety lever (canary + auto-fallback).
Samir Khan: +1. The switches idea helps productize the decisions. For launch criteria we should require: (1) canary at 10% traffic for 48h with no regressions, (2) p95 latency under SLA vs baseline, (3) rollout automation + rollback playbook.
Ravi Desai: Agree. Also add economics gate: measured cost delta per 1M tokens vs hosted baseline. Customers will push for isolation but we need to signal cost/time tradeoffs.
Hannah Li: From UX/console side we need a single toggle view: Switch state, active canaries, last rollback, and why (metrics). Minimal surface so SREs + customer PMs can see status at a glance.
Diego Morales: Ops note: make sure prefix/KV cache footprint is accounted across switches. If a tenant flips to isolated lane we need cache warm strategy or cold-start hit. Suggest feature flag to pre-warm for critical tenants.
Grace Chen: For acceptance tests: include quality checks (prompt eval suite) — isolation shouldn't degrade model outputs. If quantization or variant changes when migrating, run eval set and block rollout on regression.
Anya Patel: Good. Can we draft short acceptance checklist? I'll start:
- Canary window: 48h at >=10%
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, tokens/sec, cost delta
- Quality: no eval regression >2% on customer prompt set
- Rollback: automated fallback to compatible variant on threshold breach
- Observability: per-tenant trace and token cost visible in console
Samir Khan: Add safety thresholds: e.g., if p95 > baseline *1.2 OR error rate increase >0.5% -> immediate rollback.
Ravi Desai: Also policy precedence: local region policy should override global route, but must be explicit in the DSL. Document expected precedence table in the spec.
Hannah Li: UI note: show precedence with simple badges: region-only, tenant-override, global-fallback. Keep language non-technical for sales reviewers.
Diego Morales: We should define evacuation plan: if isolated pool hits capacity, what happens? Options: queue, degrade QoS, or fallback to dedicated shared pool. Need SLOs for each.
Grace Chen: For customer asks: some will demand 'hard isolation' (no cross-tenant co-location). We need a contract template: cost uplift + commitment window (30/90 days) and performance SLAs.
Anya Patel: Good call. I'll include contract stub in the docs. Also thinking about migration tooling: a 'migrate' op that stages traffic, warms cache, runs evals, and flips the switch.
Samir Khan: Minimal CLI sketch:
```
redwood switch set --tenant T123 --mode isolated --canary 10 --warm true
redwood switch status --tenant T123
```
Ravi Desai: Nice. Add audit logs: who flipped, why, and snapshot of active kernels/quantization variants. Compliance will ask.
Hannah Li: UX: surface a 'why' field when flipping so it's not a mystery later. Also link to the runbook.
deploy-bot: Reminder: initiative planning workshop in 30m — bring the acceptance checklist draft.
Anya Patel: I'll paste a short PR after the workshop with the 'railroad switch' diagram and the acceptance checklist. Assigning owners: Samir for rollout automation, Ravi for policy DSL precedence, Hannah for console surfaces, Diego for operational playbooks, Grace for eval gating.
Samir Khan: I'll prototype an automation flow post-workshop, aim for a spike next week.
Diego Morales: I'll mock evacuation sequences and capacity signals.
Grace Chen: I'll assemble a small eval harness for migration.
Ravi Desai: I'll start the precedence table and include examples (region > tenant > global).
Anya Patel: Great. If anyone has concrete wording for customer-facing contract line items (cost uplift %, minimum term), drop them here before EOD. :calendar:
Samir Khan: Suggest +20-30% cost uplift for hard isolation (ballpark) and minimum 60d commit. We should validate with finance.
Hannah Li: I'll draft a short one-liner for sales: "Hard isolation provides dedicated capacity with stronger SLAs; pricing is available upon request." Keep it simple.
Anya Patel: Thanks. Closing loop — will post PR with checklist + diagrams after the workshop. :thumbsup:
